function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning: The user says: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" They want to calculate the standard deviation for a null hypothesis test? Actually they give sample mean 98.2, sample std dev 1.4, sample size 40, and population mean 98.6. They want to compute the p-value? The phrase "零假設檢定的標準差" maybe means "standard deviation for the null hypothesis test"? But we have sample std dev. Maybe they want to compute the standard error? Or compute the t-statistic? The question: "計算樣本平均值為98.2、標準差為1.4、樣本大小為40的零假設檢定的標準差，以得到人口平均值為98.6。" Might be asking to compute the standard deviation of the sampling distribution under null hypothesis? That would be population standard deviation? But we only have sample std dev. Usually we use sample std dev as estimate of population std dev. So standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). That equals 1.4 / 6.3249 = 0.2215. Then t-statistic = (sample_mean - population_mean) / SE = (98.2 - 98.6)/0.2215 = -0.4/0.2215 = -1.805. Then p-value two-tailed: 2 * P(T > |t|) with df=39. We can compute approximate p-value. Let's approximate using t distribution. For t=1.805, df=39. Using t table: t(0.05) ~ 2.022, t(0.10) ~ 1.685. So p-value between 0.05 and 0.10. Roughly maybe 0.08. Let's compute more precisely: Use approximate formula: p = 2*(1 - CDF_t(1.805)). We can approximate using t distribution. But we can call the function to compute p-value. The function expects sample_mean, population_mean, sample_std_dev, sample_size, two_tailed. We'll call it.
